expected.sentence:
Death by hanging at the Columbia County Prison in Bloomsburg, Pennsylvania, on March 25, 1878.

Verdict as recorded: Yes — convicted of murder and executed by hanging.

Charges as recorded: Tried for murder as an alleged member of the Molly Maguires, in prosecutions led by Reading Railroad president Franklin B. Gowen and built largely on the testimony of the Pinkerton infiltrator James McParland.

Earlier 1868-1869 detention is separate.

expected.name: Tarek Bazrouk
expected.description: Tarek Bazrouk was a young Palestinian-American student active in New York City demonstrations concerning Israel’s war in Gaza. Federal prosecutors charged him with hate crimes for assaults on three Jewish or pro-Israel counter-demonstrators at protests in April and December 2024 and January 2025. Bazrouk pleaded guilty in June 2025, acknowledging that he selected the victims because of their Jewish religion or Israeli national origin. He had been held without release since his May 7, 2025 arrest. On October 28, 2025, U.S. District Judge Richard Berman sentenced him to seventeen months in prison followed by three years of supervised release. Palestine-solidarity organizations argued that federal intervention in matters already proceeding in state court reflected selective and politically escalated prosecution; more than 12,000 people supported a request for time served. Bazrouk was released on June 23, 2026 after 413 days in custody and completion of an early-release program.

expected.name: John Reinecke
expected.description: John Reinecke was a fired schoolteacher and Communist who was among the Hawaii Seven prosecuted under the Smith Act during the McCarthy era. He was convicted in July 1953 of conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government.
